title: Reduce Array Size to The Half
statement: You pick a set of values from the integer array `arr`, and every occurrence of each picked value is deleted from `arr`. Return the smallest number of values the set can contain so that at least half of the elements of `arr` are deleted. The length of `arr` is even.
notes:
## Intuition

Picking a value deletes as many elements as it occurs, and each pick costs the same: one more value in the set. To reach half with the fewest picks, always take the value that deletes the most elements still available, i.e. the most frequent ones first. Any other choice can be swapped for a more frequent value without deleting fewer elements, so the greedy order is optimal. Trying every subset of distinct values (the brute force) is exponential.

## Approach

1. Count how often each value occurs in the map `count`.
2. Put the counts in `frequencies` and sort them from largest to smallest; the values themselves no longer matter.
3. Take counts from the front, adding each to `removed` and increasing `chosen`, while fewer than half of the elements have been deleted (`removed * 2 < arr.length`).
4. Return `chosen`.

## Example 1, step by step

`arr = [3,3,3,3,5,5,5,2,2,7]` has 10 elements, so at least 5 must go. The counts are `3: 4`, `5: 3`, `2: 2`, `7: 1`, giving `frequencies = [4, 3, 2, 1]`. Taking 4 makes `removed = 4` (still under 5); taking 3 makes `removed = 7`, which is enough. The answer is `chosen = 2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n + d log d), where d is the number of distinct values: one counting pass plus sorting the counts.
- Space: O(d) for the map and the sorted counts.

## Pitfalls

- The goal is "at least half", so stop as soon as `removed * 2 >= arr.length`; exactly half is enough.
- Sort the counts in descending order; ascending order picks the rarest values and overcounts.
- Sort numerically with a comparator; the default `sort()` compares counts as strings (`10` before `9`).

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `count` | map from each value to how many times it occurs |
| `frequencies` | the occurrence counts, largest first |
| `removed` | number of elements deleted by the values chosen so far |
| `chosen` | number of values chosen so far (the answer) |

narration.2: This map will count how many times each value appears.
narration.4: Add one to that value's count.
narration.7: Keep only the counts, sorted largest first, since frequent values delete the most.
narration.9: And no value has been chosen yet.
narration.11: Keep choosing while fewer than half of the elements are gone.
narration.12: Choose the next most frequent value and delete all its occurrences.
narration.13: The set grows by one value.
narration.15: At least half are deleted; the number of values chosen is the minimum.
